critical_code_review_comments: safety_assessment_routes.py Level mapping is INVERTED from the review-request wording. Level 1 = 'No Direct Communication Recommended' (RED/danger, highest concern), Level 4 = 'Cooperative Co-Parenting Communication' (GREEN/safest). The review request says 'result pathway is NOT Green/Level 1' — this reads as if Level 1 were Green, which is the opposite. Recommend clarifying docs/review copy: DA-item YES escalates TO Level 1 (danger) AND away from Level 4 (Green). Product behavior is correct; only doc wording is confusing.

ai_service.py _SECTION_LENSES for 'safety' describes levels as Green/Yellow/Red, but the backend actually emits Level 1..4 with pathway_title strings. Not a bug — Claude receives whatever the caller passes in — but the internal mental model is inconsistent between the safety route (numeric 1-4) and the coaching lens (color band).

mediation_routes.py section_coaching wraps any AI failure as HTTP 500. Consider mapping upstream 429/503 from Claude to 503 with Retry-After so the frontend can retry gracefully. Low-priority hardening.

Login.jsx 'startDemo' relies on cookie-based session (no localStorage token) which is correct given AuthContext.startGuest, but note that a stray 'sac_token' check anywhere in the codebase would falsely conclude the user is not authenticated. Verified end-to-end demo flow still works via session_token cookie.
